newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-EDBERG HAS FITNESS PROBLEMS AHEAD OF DAVIS CUP SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-EDBERG HAS FITNESS PROBLEMS AHEAD OF DAVIS CUP SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Stefan Edberg, in the final year of his distinguished career, has fitness problems ahead of Sweden's Davis Cup semifinal against the Czech Republic starting in Prague on Friday.
France host Italy in Nantes on the opening day of the other semifinal with the final scheduled from November 29 to December 1.
Edberg, 30, injured an Achilles tendon at the U.S. Open this month where he was knocked out in the quarter-finals of his last grand slam appearance by Goran Ivanesevic.
"It's hard to evaluate this early in training but overall I feel fine," Edberg said.
"The foot still isn't 100 percent, it's a day-to-day situation and I hope to play in the singles. That's why I am here."
Swedish manager Carl-Axel Hageskog will monitor Edberg's progress on Wednesday but a decision may be left until shortly before Thursday's draw.
Edberg partnered Anders Jarryd 12 years ago in the crucial doubles match which gave Sweden a 4-1 victory over the United States in the Davis Cup final.
He subsequently won six major titles and a reputation as the best volleyer in the game during a career of sustained excellence which included 10 consecutive years in the world's top 10.
Edberg is scheduled to partner 14th-ranked Thomas Enqvist in the singles with Jonas Bjorkman pairing Nicklas Kulti in the doubles.
The Czech Republic upset defending champions the United States 3-2 in the quarter-finals to claim their first semifinal place for 10 years.

Their powerful left-hander Petr Korda, who partnered Edberg to the Australian doubles title this year, and the consistent Daniel Vacek head the Czech team on the fast Supreme surface at the Prague Sports Hall.
"Stefan is a player with a lot of experience," Korda said. "We've seen a lot of him and he is a tough competitor, hurt or not.
"Enqvist hits hard from both sides but I beat him on Supreme before so I have confidence."
French captain Yannick Noah has retained the team who won their first two ties 5-0 for their clash with Italy on the indoor carpet at the Palais des Sports de Beaulieu.
Cedric Pioline, world ranked 17th, will play in the singles with either Guy Forget or Arnaud Boetsch.
"I've made my choice but I'm leaving a door open," Noah said.
France have their best chance to win the Cup since Noah captained the team to an upset victory over the United States five years ago.
But, predictably, he has warned his players against complacency against the Italians who last won the Cup 20 years ago.
"To play a Davis Cup semifinal is a rare opportunity for them as well as for us," Noah said.
"They have nothing to lose and what I know for sure is that they don't fear us and are highly motivated. Extreme caution is the rule."
Italy upset Russian then South Africa in the previous two rounds but captain Adriano Panatta is gloomy about their prospects at the weekend.
"We have only a 40 percent chance of winning," he said. "Their singles players are classified much higher than ours and they are playing at home."
On paper his pessimism is justified as none of the Italian team of Renzo Furlan, Andrea Gaudenzi, Diego Nargiso and Stefano Pescosolido has got past the second round of a major tournament this year.

"I like the playing surface. It's very fast. It won't be easy but it will not be impossible to reach the final," Furlan said. Nargiso added: "Apart from in the Davis Cup, my season has been a disaster. There's nothing better than this semifinal against France to fire me up."
